transcript:
[15:00] Meeting start. Attendees: Liam Hart (Redwood AE), Priya Rao (Redwood SE), Carlos Mendez (Redwood CSM), Maya Chen (Quantaco Head of ML), Omar Ruiz (Quantaco Platform), Evelyn Park (Quantaco CTO)

Summary: quick cost econ review, looked at tokens/sec per dollar, caching savings, and batching tradeoffs. Agreed on follow-ups.

[15:02] Liam: yeah thanks everyone for joining, quick agenda — Priya will walk through the updated perf runs and the tokens per dollar model, then we can discuss caching numbers and what that means for your cost projections.

[15:03] Priya: ok cool, so we reran the benchmark on the same model family we used last week, roughly the 7B-ish open variant you gave us. baseline hosted profile (no cache) averages ~1,800 tokens/sec with our continuous batching, measured at p50; cost math we put together is about $0.35 per 1M tokens on hosted when you include infra + amortized model licensing, obviously rough.

[15:05] Maya: wait, we had earlier numbers that were closer to 2,600 tps, why the drop? did we change sequence length or batch config?

[15:06] Priya: good call — this run used a 1k average sequence length to mirror your production prompt lengths; previous run used synthetic 256 token sequences which inflated tokens/sec. with longer sequences the tokens/sec goes down, but cost per token improves a bit because there's more KV reuse.

[15:07] Omar: can you explain KV reuse again? how does prefix caching show up in costs?

[15:08] Priya: sure — so prefix/KV cache means if you have common opening prompts or system messages we keep the key/value cache and skip recomputation for that prefix. we measured typical savings of 30-55% token compute depending on prefix repetition. in one of your real workloads where 40% of calls share a 300-token system prompt, effective billable tokens dropped ~38% and tokens/sec per dollar improved accordingly.

[15:10] Evelyn: so that 38% is on compute only or on billable tokens? we need to understand what Redwood would charge vs what we measure internally.

[15:11] Priya: it's compute reduction measured on the runtime. billable depends on how you meter — in hosted mode we propose to bill on generated+input tokens but show discounts via caching credits. For the model math in the spreadsheet I attached, the cached scenario moved cost per 1M tokens from $0.35 to about $0.22 for your workload mix.

[15:12] Maya: that sounds promising. what about batching tradeoffs? in our infra we care about p95 latency — we can't let the UI feel slow.

[15:13] Priya: right. we tested three batch sizes: 1 (no batching), 8, and 32. p50 improved a lot with batch 32 but p95 worsened. numbers: batch1 p95 ~420ms, batch8 p95 ~260ms, batch32 p95 ~540ms for these long sequences. tokens/sec went from ~1,200 (batch1) to ~2,800 (batch32). so tokens/sec per dollar is highest at larger batches, but p95 violates your target of 350ms if you use very large batches.

[15:15] Omar: can we do dynamic batching? like small batches for low-latency routes and larger for async jobs?

[15:16] Priya: absolutely, that's our suggested pattern — route latency-critical traffic to a low-batch pool (dedicated smaller batch config) and route bulk/async to high-batch pools. Smart routing plus auto-fallback keeps SLAs.

[15:17] Carlos: one quick note on quantization: we tested 4-bit quantized variant which lowered GPU memory and gave similar tokens/sec but slightly higher infer variance for tail latency. it reduces cost per 1M tokens by another ~10% in dedicated scenarios.

[15:18] Maya: these are helpful. can you show the tokens/sec/$ metric? It's easier for our finance folks.

[15:19] Priya: sure — we compute tokens/sec per dollar by dividing observed tokens/sec by the hourly infra cost (converted to per-second). example: on a small dedicated GPU profile we used for testing (reference cost $2.80/hr) with batch8 we saw ~1,900 tokens/sec. tokens/sec/$ = (1900 tokens/sec) / ($2.80/hr * (1/3600 hr/sec)) which normalizes to roughly 2.4M tokens per dollar per second window — to keep it simple, the spreadsheet shows tokens per dollar per hour and cost per 1M tokens.

[15:21] Liam: bottom line — hosted with caching gives you easiest path and ~35-45% cost savings over naive hosted; dedicated + quantization can get another 20-30% savings if you commit capacity. but dedicated adds ops complexity and minimum commit.

[15:22] Evelyn: and what about fallback behavior if dedicated pool saturates? we need to ensure availability and consistent latency.

[15:23] Priya: smart routing will fail over to a compatible hosted variant or different region; you can set timeouts and automatic degradation (smaller model family) or return cached responses for high-hit prefixes. that's part of the rollout policy. it will increase cost if we route to hosted fallback but keeps the app online.

[15:25] Omar: a practical ask — can we see a longer run test with real traffic patterns? bursts, long-tail prompts, and sustained 6-hour run. our production shape has heavy evening peaks.

[15:26] Priya: yes — action item for us to run a 6-hour benchmark with your sample logs if you share them. We'll capture p50/p95/p99, cache hit-rate over time, and cost delta.

[15:27] Maya: also please include per-route breakdown — our chat feature vs internal summarization have very different latency budgets and caching patterns.

[15:28] Liam: quick recap before we close — Priya to share updated perf runs and spreadsheet by Friday; Priya to run longer caching benchmark once Quantaco supplies sample logs; Maya to surface top prefixes; Liam to send pricing/dedicated options and SLA.

[15:30] Evelyn: one more thing — security/compliance ask: we will need SOC2 and encryption key flow doc for private deployment decision. can we get that?

[15:31] Carlos: yes I'll attach the SOC2 summary and KMS/HSM integration doc to the notes, and we can set a security call next week if needed.

[15:33] Maya: sounds good, thanks.

[15:34] Meeting end.
